explanation:
[EFFECT] The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic (double-peaked) effect on predicted bike demand. Contributions are deeply negative in the pre-dawn hours, reaching their lowest point around 4–5 AM, meaning demand is heavily suppressed at those times. There are two clear peaks where the hour boosts demand the most: a morning peak around 8 AM and an even stronger evening peak around 5 PM (17:00), both corresponding to typical commuter rush hours. After the evening peak, contributions steadily fall back into negative territory by 11 PM–midnight.

[IMPORTANCE] The hour of the day is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9 with an importance score of 0.833 — substantially higher than all other features. It has by far the largest influence on how many bikes are predicted to be rented in any given hour.

[RECOMMENDATION] Staffing levels, bike redistribution, and dock capacity should be closely aligned with the two daily demand peaks around 8 AM and 5 PM, while maintenance and rebalancing operations are best scheduled in the early morning hours (roughly 3–5 AM) when demand is at its lowest.
